justification: Stops test runs writing to the production database; no served output changes, one guard in the commit worker.

pre_impl.existing_data: regulatory_provisions citation_status and page_check verdicts, written by the post-publish re-check scripts.
pre_impl.assumption_mismatch: If PYTEST_CURRENT_TEST is set outside pytest, the re-checks are skipped and the health checks (DQ-113, citation) report the unchecked rows.
pre_impl.new_vs_existing: Only changes behaviour inside pytest; production publishes run the re-checks exactly as before.

functions.name: main
functions.input: command line flags and the approved review queue rows from the database
functions.output: committed provisions, then per-council post-publish re-check subprocesses
functions.if_none: with no committed councils nothing is re-checked, as before

values.if_missing: unset outside pytest, so production runs the re-checks

break_it.scenario: A test drives main() with a fake connection and commits a council
break_it.what_happens: the re-check scripts start as subprocesses with the real .env and write verdicts to production
break_it.how: scripts/dcp_commit_approved.py:675 skips them when PYTEST_CURRENT_TEST is set
break_it.repro: run the three commit-worker test files and count backup files: unchanged

break_it.scenario: The guard also fires in a production publish
break_it.what_happens: verdicts would go stale after a publish
break_it.how: PYTEST_CURRENT_TEST is set only by pytest; the migration 079 and 078 triggers void stale verdicts and the health checks fail on unchecked rows

break_it.scenario: A new post-publish script is added outside the guarded loop
break_it.what_happens: tests reach production again through the new subprocess
break_it.how: tests/test_dcp_page_repair.py pins the guard on the loop that holds every re-check

falsifiable_check.fails_when: a new backup file appears, meaning a subprocess wrote to production
falsifiable_check.observed_red: 2026-09-27: before the guard, a pre-push test run left ten backup files 0354-0403, one recording a 1,290-row write; after it, the same three files ran with the count unchanged (14 before, 14 after) and in 4.5s instead of 24s.
